moved.sentence: From Kent Beck's Test Desiderata — tests should be:

judged.note: The rationale keeps the attribution to Kent Beck's Test Desiderata and that these are properties tests should have; every listed property is a rule at SHOULD or MUST.

moved.sentence: **Isolated** — tests MUST NOT share mutable state or depend on execution order

judged.note: Kept at MUST NOT: no shared mutable state and no dependence on execution order.

moved.sentence: **Composable** — tests MUST be runnable in any subset and any order

judged.note: Kept at MUST: runnable in any subset and any order.

moved.sentence: **Deterministic** — tests MUST produce the same result every time, no flakiness

judged.note: Kept at MUST: same result every time, no flakiness.

moved.sentence: **Fast** — milliseconds per unit test, seconds per integration test

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD (the list's 'should be') with both speed targets.
Kept at SHOULD: easy to author, low ceremony.

moved.sentence: **Readable** — a failing test tells you what broke and why

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: a failing test tells you what broke and why.

moved.sentence: **Behavioral** — tests SHOULD verify what the code does, not how it does it

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: verify what the code does, not how.

moved.sentence: **Structure-insensitive** — refactoring internals SHOULD NOT break tests

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD NOT: refactoring internals does not break tests.

moved.sentence: **Automated** — no manual steps, no human judgment needed

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: no manual steps, no human judgment.

moved.sentence: **Specific** — a failure points to exactly one cause

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: a failure points to exactly one cause.

moved.sentence: **Predictive** — passing tests mean the code works in production

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: passing tests mean the code works in production.
Kept at SHOULD: confidence to refactor and ship.
